Academic Research Project

Malicious URL Detection Using Machine Learning

A structured investigation into modern multi-layer phishing campaigns like Oktapus, leveraging unified lexical, host, and SSL infrastructure feature spaces to provide real-time zero-day mitigation.

THE PROBLEM

Targeted Identity Harvesting

Traditional blocklists (Google Safe Browsing, DNS blocklists) suffer from an average latency of 2 to 6 hours before newly registered phishing hostnames are reported. Threat groups like Oktapus take advantage of this golden window by circulating ephemeral SMS links that expire before blocklists can index them.

THE OBJECTIVE

Feature-Based Predictive Zero-Day Classification

Rather than relying on retroactive domain reputations, URLGuard parses the structural anatomy of the string itself, quantifying Shannon entropy, subdomain clustering, keyword mimicry vectors, and SSL metadata to identify credential harvesters on their very first request.

8-Step Machine Learning Pipeline

End-to-end data ingestion, normalization, feature extraction, and inference

STEP 01
URL Parsing & RFC 3986

Tokenize schemes, domain, TLD, query, parameters, and fragments.

STEP 02
Character Normalization

Punycode conversion, percent-encoding decoding, and homoglyph resolution.

STEP 03
Lexical Feature Extraction

Length, entropy, delimiter distribution, vowel/consonant balance.

STEP 04
Brand Mimicry Scoring

Levenshtein distance calculation against top 100 enterprise IdP domains.

STEP 05
Host & DNS Telemetry

Subdomain depth count, DynDNS recognition, and ASN lookup.

STEP 06
SSL Lifespan Analysis

CA authority tier, ephemeral validity windows, and SAN wildcard checks.

STEP 07
Random Forest Ensemble

500 decision trees evaluate 54 vector features with probability aggregation.

STEP 08
Companion Figurine State

Mascot translates mathematical probability into clear expressive risk signaling.
